analysis.title: Prime Insights & Analytics Chart Pack – Fundamental L/S Net Exposure Below Liberation Day lows. Value Rotation.
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S managers are down 0.2% in November so far and up 8.9% YTD as of Nov 16. Beta losses were partly offset by positive alpha from short-side gains. Systematic L/S is up 1.1% MTD after a sharp recovery last week.
TMT and Asia L/S funds are under the most performance pressure, down 4.5% and 1.4% MTD respectively.
Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities in November, with long and short sales at about 3 to 1. Single stocks were net sold in 7 of the last 8 weeks and the pace has picked up MTD.
ETF short flows have become more volatile, which the desk reads as investors using macro products to hedge and manage exposure.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell another 7.6 pts MTD to its lowest level in more than five years, now below the Liberation Day lows.
After persistent de-grossing and heavy net selling, the desk says equities could set up for a tactical rally in the near term as seasonality and technicals become friendlier.
GIR's Sentiment Indicator and Risk Appetite Indicator do not show depressed positioning across a broader set of market participants, which limits the read from hedge fund positioning alone.
EM Asia and North America were heavily net sold in November, outpacing modest net buying in Europe and DM Asia. Taiwan, Korea and China were the most net sold Asian markets MTD.
Hedge funds are overweight Asia (DM + EM) by 8.4% relative to MSCI World ACWI, versus a record high of 20% in June and 6.5% at the start of 2026.
Selling in global Info Tech over the trailing 6 weeks since early October is the fastest in the past decade (-4.4 z score), led by Semis and Semi Equipment.

Industrials is the second most net sold US sector MTD behind Info Tech, with net exposure at its lowest level in more than two years. Consumer Staples is also among the most net sold US sectors, which suggests managers are fading its price rally.
Hedge funds have cut risk in US Health Care for 9 consecutive weeks, and Biotech de-grossing accelerated in November, driven by long sales.
Exposure to Medium-Term Momentum is on track to fall for a 6th straight month to the lowest since Dec 2022. Exposure to Value has risen sharply to 5-year highs amid stagflation concerns.

Stagflation concerns are driving the rotation into Value.
